name: Castell de Sant Ferran, Figueres (last Cortes)
story: As Catalonia collapsed, the Republican government withdrew to Figueres. On 1 February 1939 Prime Minister Juan Negrín held the last session of the Republican Cortes on Spanish soil in the stables of this huge 18th-century fortress, proposing peace conditions that Franco ignored. The castle and places nearby also sheltered art evacuated from the Prado and other collections before it was sent to Geneva. Days later the government crossed into France and Nationalist troops reached the border on 10 February. From 1940 to 1942 the Franco regime used the castle as a concentration camp for Republicans returned from France.
see: One of the largest bastioned fortresses in Europe: the stables where the Cortes met, the parade ground, bastions and underground cisterns.
plan: On the edge of Figueres, 20 minutes' walk from the Dalí Museum; check seasonal hours. Guided visits to the underground cisterns (by boat) and the moat (by electric vehicle) must be booked.
